handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

what_was_done_this_session.scale_metric_model_clarified: MAJOR conceptual work this session (see memories). (a) Cost is NOT normalizable by any single metric (not road_LF, not a lumped earthwork CY). It decomposes into independent components, each scaling off its OWN driver, summed: road corridor (road_LF) + site/lot work (lot area × stripping depth) + per-lot (lot_count). (b) Site work is AREAL not deep-volume — digging out lots is mostly shallow topsoil stripping + grade-to-fit, so site_CY ≈ area_SF × strip_depth/27; cost tracks AREA at ~fixed depth. (c) A single lumped 'earthwork CY' misleads because deep road/trench CY and broad shallow strip CY are different work at different unit costs — keep them separate.
what_was_done_this_session.ROW_SF_is_not_lot_axis: CONFIRMED empirically on Expo: ROW_SF (right-of-way SF) = the PUBLIC ROAD CORRIDOR (road + sidewalks + planter), so ROW_SF ≈ road_LF × ROW_width and is COLLINEAR with road_LF — NOT an independent lot-area metric. Nolan's hand-calc ROW area 28,750 SF ≈ parsed ROW_SF 32,674. The lot-dig axis is currently UNMEASURED. Also confirmed: the qty sheet 'ROW STRIPPING' line is ROW-ONLY, not whole-site (Expo single lot = 178,882 SF vs ROW STRIPPING qty of only 1,815). So lot disturbance area must be sourced as a NEW metric lot_area_SF off the plat; lot EXCAVATION work itself is already present as proposal/qty cut-fill CY line items (Expo gap audit was clean), only its normalizing area is missing.
what_was_done_this_session.jobtype_from_signatures: Decision: job_type should be INFERRED from the measurement signature (e.g. lot_area_SF >> ROW_SF -> lot-dig/pad job like Expo; lot_area_SF comparable to ROW_SF -> road/subdivision), NOT hand-coded. Keep manifest job_type as a ground-truth ANCHOR while data is sparse (8 jobs can't calibrate thresholds); let M2 LEARN the threshold ranges as job count grows.

The road_LF-reading memory captures Nolan's full plan-reading playbook (see key_findings).

key_findings_and_decisions: SCALE-METRIC MODEL: cost = sum of independent components, each normalized by its own driver (road_LF for corridor; lot_area x strip_depth for site; lot_count per-lot). No single normalizer. Site work is areal/shallow, not deep volume. This drives how M2 builds unit-rate distributions — segment PER COMPONENT, not one $/total.

ROW_SF = road corridor, collinear with road_LF (confirmed Expo 28,750 hand vs 32,674 parsed). It does NOT capture lot/site area. NEW metric needed: lot_area_SF (and/or total disturbed SF), hand/vision-read from the plat. Add to schema + manifest when the vision pass starts.
'ROW STRIPPING' in the qty sheet is ROW-only (Expo: lot 178,882 SF >> stripping 1,815). The whole-site/lot disturbance is NOT in the qty sheet stripping line.
job_type inferred from metric signatures (ratios), manifest label kept as anchor; thresholds learned in M2.

Statistical pattern mining (correlation/covariance across qty-sheet quantities + proposal line items) is the planned M2 engine to DERIVE the decomposition and job-type signatures empirically — analogous to the HeavyBid pattern work. CAVEAT: 8 jobs is too few; exploratory until ~50-job RAG threshold.

ROAD_LF PLAN-READING PLAYBOOK (Nolan's method, now in memory project_reading_road_lf_from_plans): (1) stationing labels are primary, LF = end_sta - start_sta; (2) road-name title sometimes carries the segment length; (3) PROFILE view is most reliable — start/stop shown explicitly via 'begin'/'start' labels, or dotted(existing)->bold(proposed) transition, or whole x-axis span if entire road is built; (4) plan-view stationing cross-checks the profile, read left->right then top->down, beware round 10+00/11+00 that may be existing; (5) solid/bold = proposed work zone (plan=area, profile=elevation); (6) multi-road jobs: identify which road via road name, adjacent names, compass orientation, similar labels, and assume the main road is horizontal — single roads often broken to one-per-page later in the set, SUM all segments; (7) some plans give an explicit LF callout (used for Expo -> road_LF_source 'plan_callout').

OPEN PROBLEM (#9): some plans tie into EXISTING roads — how does an AI determine which roads are existing vs proposed and whether work is actually required? Dotted->bold transition is the main visual tell but needs a robust rule before road_LF extraction can be automated. Until solved, road_LF stays hand-read (manifest-authoritative).
